finding.title: Register a vulnerability
finding.subtitle: A record anyone can replay: what it is, where it lives, how we got in, what proves it.
finding.section.validation: What we expected and what happened
finding.hint.what: The name whoever fixes it will search for, and the weakness class (CWE) so it is not an invented label.
finding.hint.cwe: The real class. An IDOR is CWE-639, not "broken access control".
finding.hint.where: The product is the crown jewel, not the domain that serves it. The endpoint is the exact route, parameters included.
finding.hint.asset: Search the domain to tie the finding to an inventory asset.
finding.hint.url: The service's base URL, the way the client writes it.
finding.hint.endpoint: The path only: /api/v1/invoices/1042 — query string exactly as you sent it.
finding.hint.auth: If a session is needed, pick the profile you already used. It is created once and every finding of the engagement reuses it.
finding.hint.authProfile: The profile stores headers or login steps, never a plaintext password.
finding.hint.proof: Paste the raw request and response (Burp: Copy to file). This is what lets somebody else replay it without asking you.
finding.hint.request: Method, host, headers and body. No live token: mask it.
finding.hint.response: Status, relevant headers and the fragment that proves the effect.
finding.hint.validation: No output means no validation: the expected, the observed, and the concrete trace that proves it.
finding.hint.output: The observable evidence: status code, error, another user's data, timing.
finding.hint.reproduction: Numbered, with the session profile and the minimum to repeat it.
finding.hint.claim: Enters as a claim: a person confirms it, not the act of writing it.
finding.hint.profileHeaders: Headers that authenticate the session, one per line.
finding.hint.profileSteps: How the session is obtained: endpoint, test credentials and what it returns.
finding.field.name: name
finding.hint.project: The product this belongs to. A record without an owner is a note nobody can route.
finding.hint.cycle: Optional: the engagement that produced it. Naming one puts the claim in that cycle's ledger.
finding.hint.build: The exact release, when the claim was seen in one. A pentest against 1.4.0 is not the same claim as one against main.
finding.placeholder.name: IDOR at /api/v1/invoices/{id}
finding.placeholder.output: HTTP 200 · 42 KB · invoice 1042 of another user
finding.placeholder.impact: Any authenticated customer reads another's invoices.
finding.placeholder.reproduction:
1. log in as A
2. GET /api/v1/invoices/1042 with A's cookie
finding.error.title: It needs a name: that is what whoever fixes it will search for.
finding.error.subject: It needs a subject: pick the product, the asset or the cycle it came from.
findingPage.request.title: The request it claims
findingPage.request.loginHint: The Repeat tab sends the login first and carries the token forward — no header to paste.
findingPage.repeat.lead: Send the request again, with the login it needs: a step can extract a value (token = json:authentication.token) and a later one uses it as {{token}}.
findingPage.repeat.extractHint: one per line: name = json:path | header:name | regex:pattern
findingPage.repeat.result.denied: Stopped: a step is not authorized
findingPage.repeat.result.error: Stopped: {n} step(s), one did not complete
findingPage.repeat.empty.title: No run yet
findingPage.repeat.empty.hint: Send the chain and the request/response pair is kept here: the run is the evidence, not the screenshot.
